text: Reproduce Bloch's counting set, where both overrides are correct and the answer is wrong. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: @Override public boolean add(E e) { ___; return super.add(e); }
@Override public boolean addAll(Collection<? extends E> c) { ___; return super.addAll(c); }
explanation: Verified: `6 3`. Three elements added, counter says six. `HashSet.addAll` is implemented by calling `add`, so the override counts each element twice — and no documentation was obliged to mention that, and a future version may change it. There is no version of this class that is correct against `HashSet` as specified, which is the sharpest available argument against casual inheritance.
